description: Add a defensive decoy response for hostile 404s. When a request would result in a 404, and the path is NOT one that 'might have been valid' (well-formed image path, or a valid-shaped flight-card/event path that just doesn't exist), and is NOT from a logged-in user, and is NOT a standard web file (anything under /.well-known/ or /robots.txt and similar), return the decoy body 'these are not the droids you are looking for'. 10% of the time (probabilistically) return a gzip bomb instead of the plain message; the other 90% return the plain message. All other 404s (exempted cases) must keep their normal existing behavior.
steps: Create a new module flight_card_scanner/middleware/decoy_middleware.py containing the decoy logic as pure, unit-testable helper functions plus a middleware/handler entry point. Keep decision logic in standalone functions so tests can call them directly without spinning up the whole app.

Implement a helper `is_exempt_path(path: str) -> bool` that returns True for standard web files and 'might-have-been-valid' paths. Standard web files: path == '/robots.txt', path == '/favicon.ico', path == '/sitemap.xml', and any path starting with '/.well-known/'. 'Might have been valid': (a) a well-formed image path, i.e. the path ends with a common image extension (.png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .webp, .svg, .ico) case-insensitively, OR sits under an event image route (contains '/images/'); (b) a valid-shaped event / flight-card path, i.e. path == '/' or starts with '/events/' (these are legitimately-shaped routes that simply may not resolve to an existing event/record), and also the known top-level app routes ('/login','/logout','/register','/lost-rockets','/admin','/static'). Add clear comments explaining each branch. These exempted paths must receive the ORIGINAL 404 response, never the decoy.

Implement `build_decoy_response(rng=None) -> Response` (or an async equivalent) that: with probability 0.10 returns a gzip bomb and with probability 0.90 returns a plain-text response whose body is EXACTLY the bytes of 'these are not the droids you are looking for' (exact string, no extra punctuation/newline changes; media_type text/plain). Use a seedable/injectable RNG parameter (e.g. accept a random.Random or a probability source) so tests can force each branch deterministically. Use HTTP status 200 for the decoy (a normal-looking response for the attacker), not 404 - the whole point is to not reveal the 404. Document this choice in a comment.

Implement the gzip bomb safely: construct a Response with body = gzip-compressed bytes of a highly compressible payload (e.g. a large run of a single byte such as b'\0' * N or b'0' * N where N is large enough to be a meaningful decompression bomb, e.g. on the order of tens of MB decompressed, but the COMPRESSED payload stays tiny). Set header 'Content-Encoding: gzip' and 'Content-Type: text/plain' (or application/octet-stream) and DO NOT set a conflicting Content-Length that contradicts the compressed body (let Starlette compute it from the actual compressed bytes). Compress with Python's gzip/zlib. Keep the in-memory work bounded on the server side (compressing zeros is cheap and the compressed output is tiny); do NOT materialize the full decompressed payload in server memory. Add a module-level constant for the decompressed size and a comment noting the bomb is only dangerous to a client that auto-decompresses.

Wire it into the app in flight_card_scanner/main.py as a new global HTTP middleware. It must run the request via call_next, inspect the resulting response; if response.status_code == 404 AND request.state.user is None (not logged in) AND not is_exempt_path(request.url.path), replace the response with build_decoy_response(); otherwise return the original response untouched. CRITICAL ordering: this middleware needs request.state.user to already be set by the existing session_resolution middleware. In Starlette the LAST-added @app.middleware('http') runs OUTERMOST (first on the request). Register the decoy middleware so that session_resolution runs BEFORE it: i.e. add the decoy middleware function in the source ABOVE (before) the existing session_resolution @app.middleware definition, or otherwise guarantee session_resolution executes first and populates request.state.user. Defensively handle the case where request.state.user attribute may be missing (getattr(request.state, 'user', None)).
Ensure logged-in users are fully exempt: if request.state.user is not None, always return the original 404 (e.g. the normal JSON 404 or 404.html) so authenticated users get real error pages.

Add tests in tests/test_decoy_404.py. Model the app-construction and client usage on tests/test_multi_event_routing.py (build a small FastAPI app, add a session-resolution-like middleware that sets request.state.user, add the decoy middleware, register a couple of real routes plus rely on unmatched routes for 404, and use httpx.AsyncClient with ASGITransport). Cover: (1) a clearly-bogus unmatched path for an anonymous user returns 200 with body exactly 'these are not the droids you are looking for' when RNG forces the 90% branch; (2) same bogus path returns a gzip-bomb response (Content-Encoding: gzip, body decompresses to the large payload) when RNG forces the 10% branch - verify by decompressing and checking length/content; (3) a logged-in user hitting the same bogus path gets a normal 404 (NOT the decoy body); (4) '/robots.txt' and a '/.well-known/...' path get the normal 404, not the decoy; (5) a well-formed-but-missing image path (e.g. '/events/2026/nxrs/images/does-not-exist.jpg' or a bare '/something.png') gets the normal 404, not the decoy; (6) a valid-shaped-but-missing event path (e.g. '/events/nope/nope/') gets the normal 404, not the decoy. Force the RNG branch deterministically via the injectable RNG parameter or by monkeypatching the probability source; do NOT rely on real randomness in assertions. Also add direct unit tests for is_exempt_path and build_decoy_response.

Also add at least one probabilistic sanity unit test that calls build_decoy_response many times with a real RNG and asserts the gzip-bomb fraction is roughly 10% (loose bounds, e.g. between 3% and 20% over 1000 draws) to document the intended ratio without being flaky.
acceptance_criteria: An anonymous request to a clearly-bogus 404 path returns HTTP 200 whose body is exactly the bytes 'these are not the droids you are looking for' in the non-bomb branch.
In the bomb branch the response has Content-Encoding: gzip and its body decompresses to the configured large highly-compressible payload, while the compressed body on the wire is small.
The gzip-bomb branch occurs with ~10% probability and the plain message ~90%, controllable deterministically in tests via an injected RNG.
Logged-in users (request.state.user is not None) always receive the original 404, never the decoy.
Standard web files (/robots.txt, /.well-known/*, /favicon.ico, /sitemap.xml) receive the original 404, never the decoy.
'Might-have-been-valid' paths (well-formed image paths, and valid-shaped '/events/...' or '/' paths) receive the original 404, never the decoy.
python3.12 -m pytest tests/test_decoy_404.py -q passes all new tests.
The full suite shows no NEW failures beyond the 5 documented pre-existing baseline failures.
findings: Implemented flight_card_scanner/middleware/decoy_middleware.py (pure helpers is_exempt_path + build_decoy_response, gzip bomb 50MiB decompressed / tiny compressed, decoy returns HTTP 200, injectable RNG) and wired decoy_hostile_404 into main.py ABOVE session_resolution so session_resolution runs outermost and populates request.state.user first. Added tests/test_decoy_404.py (40 tests, all pass) modeled on test_multi_event_routing.py. Test note: a bare /events/{path}/ route 307-redirects when the URL lacks a trailing slash, so the test app uses follow_redirects=True and a dedicated .../images/{filename} route to exercise the missing-image 404 case. REVIEW-FIX (2026-09-05-090507 review, NEEDS_CHANGES): addressed all 4 issues. (1) Precompute the gzip-bomb compressed payload once at import into module-level _BOMB_COMPRESSED_BYTES instead of allocating b'\0'*50MiB and re-running DEFLATE on every bomb response; _build_gzip_bomb_response now just reuses the constant, so hostile bursts no longer amplify into server memory/CPU. (2) Removed '/admin' from _KNOWN_TOP_LEVEL_ROUTES: there is no top-level /admin route (admin is under /events/{event_path}/api/admin/..., already covered by the /events/ exemption), so a bare /admin probe now correctly gets the decoy instead of an honest 404; updated tests to assert /admin and /admin/users are NOT exempt. (3)+(4) Gave the production decoy_404_middleware an optional injectable rng param threaded through to build_decoy_response, and rewrote the test _build_app so the forced-RNG e2e path now drives the REAL decoy_404_middleware (passing rng=rng) instead of re-implementing its body inline; this exercises the production entrypoint end-to-end on both the plain and bomb branches. Verification: tests/test_decoy_404.py = 40 passed; full suite = 590 passed, 5 failed (exactly the documented pre-existing failures: test_audit_service append_mode, test_bedrock_endpoint api_failure, and 3 test_event_manager open/get cases). No new failures/regressions.
